comparisons.peer_summary: AMD agreed to acquire ZT Group Int'l, Inc. (ZT Systems) in August 2024 to extend data center infrastructure capabilities and accelerate time to market for AI solutions, with expected closure in the first half of fiscal 2025 subject to regulatory approvals and intent to seek a strategic partner for ZT's manufacturing business.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD describe strategic actions to extend their data center infrastructure capabilities specifically to accelerate AI solutions and time-to-market for customers. Intel’s DCAI segment focuses on delivering workload-optimized solutions and silicon devices to address complex challenges for its customer base, including cloud providers and enterprises. AMD similarly acquired ZT Systems, a provider of AI and general-purpose compute infrastructure, explicitly stating that this acquisition is intended to accelerate time to market for its AI training and inferencing solutions. While Intel emphasizes its existing portfolio breadth, AMD highlights the acquisition as the mechanism to extend infrastructure capabilities.

sentences.text: DCAI delivers innovative workload-optimized solutions to cloud service providers and enterprises, along with silicon devices for communications service providers, network and edge, and HPC customers.
Our unique capabilities enable us to help solve our customers' most complex challenges with the depth and breadth of our hardware and software portfolio.

We also focused on extending our data center infrastructure capabilities by entering into an agreement in August 2024 to acquire ZT Group Int'l, Inc. (ZT Systems), a provider of AI and general purpose compute infrastructure for hyperscale computing companies.
We believe that with the acquisition of ZT Systems, we can accelerate time to market for our leadership AI training and inferencing solutions.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center Revenue and AI Inference
comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $47.5 billion, up 217% from fiscal year 2023, with approximately 40% estimated to be for AI inference. In the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2024, large cloud providers represented more than half of this revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies provide specific details regarding their Data Center business performance in the fiscal year 2024, highlighting the scale of their operations and customer base. Intel identifies its Data Center and AI (DCAI) segment as serving cloud service providers, enterprises, and HPC customers with workload-optimized solutions. NVIDIA reports $47.5 billion in Data Center revenue, noting that large cloud providers represented more than half of this revenue, supporting both internal workloads and external customers. Both disclosures confirm that large cloud providers are a critical component of their respective Data Center revenue streams and customer ecosystems.
